content.title: About
content.content: High‑protein toasted bread is a whole‑grain loaf enriched with plant‑based or whey protein. After toasting it develops a crunchy crust while staying soft inside, offering a rich, nutty aroma.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Athletes and diet‑conscious people often choose high‑protein bread to boost daily protein intake.
Toasting intensifies flavor and crunch without significantly reducing nutrients.
Recipes may include sunflower, pumpkin or flax seeds, further increasing protein and healthy fat content.
This bread typically has a lower glycemic index than regular white bread.
Manufacturers use a slow‑mixing dough process to improve gluten structure and retain more protein.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Each slice provides about 10–12 g of protein, supporting muscle maintenance and post‑workout recovery.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: The whole‑grain base supplies fiber that aids digestion and satiety.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Toasted bread raises blood sugar more slowly, which is beneficial for weight management and diabetes control.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: B1, B2 and B3 vitamins help with energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Contains essential minerals
items.content: Magnesium, iron and zinc support muscle function and immune health.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: People with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity should avoid this product.

items.title: High calorie density
items.content: Because of added protein and seeds, a slice can contain up to 250 kcal; portion control is advised.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some versions contain added salt; choose low‑sodium options if you have hypertension.

items.title: Added additives
items.content: Certain recipes use artificial sweeteners or preservatives; check the label if you avoid them.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Toasted high‑protein bread works well for sandwiches with lean meat, cottage cheese, avocado or hummus. Use it as a base for open‑face toast, a side for soups, or simply as a crunchy snack.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the bread in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 3–4 days. For longer storage, refrigerate or freeze individual slices and re‑toast before eating.

content.title: About
content.content: A cheeseburger is a classic fast‑food item consisting of a beef patty, melted cheese, pickles, onions, lettuce, and sauce sandwiched between a split bun. In the NFS (1661) version a special beef blend and a signature sauce give the burger a richer flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first cheeseburger was served in the 1920s in the United States.
In NFS (1661) the bun is lightly topped with sesame seeds, distinguishing it from standard versions.
The cheese used is processed cheddar, which melts faster than traditional cheese slices.
Cheeseburgers are often used in advertising as a symbol of quick, affordable food.
Some markets add bacon, but the original NFS (1661) recipe does not include it.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: The beef patty provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Red meat is rich in heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: Melted cheese adds calcium, important for bone and teeth health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Beef and cheese supply B12, B6, and niacin, supporting nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Energy boost
items.content: The combination of protein, fat, and carbohydrates quickly replenishes energy stores.

items.title: High fat and calorie content
items.content: Cheeseburgers can be calorie‑dense and contain saturated fats, so they should be eaten in moderation.

items.title: Sodium levels
items.content: Sauces and cheese add significant salt, which may be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: People with lactose intolerance or milk protein allergy should choose dairy‑free alternatives.

items.title: Foodborne illness risk
items.content: Undercooked beef patties may harbor harmful bacteria; ensure the patty is fully cooked.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cheeseburgers are typically eaten by hand, holding the bottom bun. They can be split in half for easier sharing. Adding fresh vegetables such as tomato or lettuce can lighten the taste.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store a prepared cheeseburger in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours in an airtight container. Reheat in an oven or microwave to keep the bun from getting soggy. Do not keep for more than 2 days to avoid spoilage.

content.title: About
content.content: Dove is a line of skin‑care products developed by Unilever. Dove items are known for their gentle formula that contains ¼ cream, providing deep moisturisation and skin protection. The range includes soaps, shower gels, lotions and creams suitable for daily use.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first Dove soap was launched in 1957 in the United States.
The brand positions itself around "Real Beauty", featuring people of diverse ages, body types and ethnicities in its advertising.
Dove formulas often contain microscopic ceramide particles that help restore the skin’s natural barrier.
Dove products are sold in more than 80 countries worldwide.
Unilever supports confidence‑building programs for teenagers through the "Real Beauty" initiative.

items.title: Moisturising
items.content: The ¼ cream content helps retain water in the outer epidermal layers, leaving skin soft and smooth.

items.title: Barrier protection
items.content: Ceramides and mild surfactants aid in rebuilding the skin’s natural barrier, reducing irritation.

items.title: Suitable for sensitive skin
items.content: Hypoallergenic formulas without strong fragrances make Dove a good choice for people with sensitive skin.

items.title: Reduces dryness
items.content: Regular use can lessen the feeling of tightness and flakiness after showering.

items.title: Soothing effect
items.content: Some variants contain aloe and vitamin E, which calm irritated skin.

items.title: Allergy to ingredients
items.content: A small number of individuals may experience allergic reactions to fragrances or preservatives used in certain Dove products.

items.title: Excessive moisturisation
items.content: For very oily skin, frequent use of cream‑rich formulas may increase greasiness.

items.title: Eye contact
items.content: Shower gels can cause eye irritation if they get into the eyes; rinse thoroughly.

items.title: Storage
items.content: Keep products in a dry place away from direct sunlight to prevent fragrance degradation.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Apply soap or gel to wet skin, lather, and rinse with warm water. After showering, apply lotions or creams to dry skin, massaging gently until fully absorbed. For best results, use products from the same line together.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store Dove products in their original packaging in a cool, dry place protected from direct sunlight. Keep caps tightly closed to avoid loss of fragrance.

content.title: About
content.content: Hard pretzels with cheese filling are baked snack sticks shaped into traditional knots, made from wheat flour, salt and yeast, and filled with melted cheese. They have a crunchy crust, a soft interior and a rich cheesy flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pretzels originated in Europe where they were traditionally twisted into knot shapes.
The cheese filling often blends cheddar with processed cheese for a distinctive aroma.
Hard pretzels are commonly served as a snack with beer and fast‑food meals.
In the United States more than 200 million packages of pretzels are sold each year.
One legend says the knot shape symbolizes crossed hands in prayer.

items.title: Source of carbohydrates
items.content: Pretzels provide quick‑release carbs that supply energy for active tasks.

items.title: Protein content
items.content: The cheese filling adds a modest amount of dairy and plant protein.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: The cheese layer contributes calcium, important for bones and teeth.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Wheat flour contains B1, B2 and niacin, supporting metabolism.

items.title: Iron
items.content: Pretzels can help maintain iron levels in the body.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Pretzels made from wheat flour may trigger reactions in people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: High sodium
items.content: The salty crust makes the product high in sodium; those with hypertension should limit intake.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Cheese filling raises the calorie count, so portions should be moderate.

items.title: Lactose
items.content: The cheese may contain lactose, which is relevant for lactose‑intolerant individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pretzels are convenient as a standalone snack, paired with dips (cheese, mustard, tomato) or added to salads and soups for crunch.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in a sealed package in a cool, dry place. For longer storage, refrigerate to maintain crispness and prevent staling.
